newsitem.title: FRANCE: France mum on whether Mobutu welcome on its soil.
newsitem.headline: France mum on whether Mobutu welcome on its soil.

text.p: An embarrassed France kept its council on Monday on whether deposed Zairean leader Mobutu Sese Seko would be welcome on French soil amidst media speculation he would seek asylum only after France's parliamentary election.
"We do not know Mr Mobutu's intentions," a foreign ministry spokesman said.

Paris was unaware of Mobutu's current whereabouts and had not heard from the former Zairean president since he fled his ancestral home at Gbadolite, just ahead of Laurent Kabila's rebel soldiers, the spokesman said.
A senior Moroccan security official said on Sunday that Mobutu and his family had arrived in Morocco and were staying at a hotel on the coast south of Rabat.
France, which supported Mobutu long after other Western nations had dropped him, had grudgingly acknowledged on Saturday Kabila's takeover of the central African state.
Mobutu's downfall was widely seen as a setback for the conservative government at the height of a parliamentary election campaign.
"It is obvious that it would be difficult (for Mobutu) to fly right away to the Cote d'Azur, since France is in the midst of an election campaign," the daily France-Soir said in a typical comment.
France's two-round parliamentary election takes place on May 25 and June 1.

"Even more so in that a representative of Kabila has declared that it would be considered 'an unfriendly act' for France to welcome Mobutu on its soil," the newspaper said under the headline, "Mobutu in France? Not right away".

A Kabila spokesman had threatened on Sunday to "plant bombs" in France should it give shelter to Mobutu. The spokesman had also demanded that the ousted president's property in the country be turned over to Zaire's new government.
The foreign ministry spokesman said he would have no comment on the threats.

Asked if Paris might rule out asylum for Mobutu in France, where he owns a palatial Riviera villa, the spokesman said the question could only be answered if and when Mobutu sought permission to come here.

Asked if Mobutu was able to enter France without official permission, as he had done regularly in recent months, the spokesman said he could not give a definitive answer but expected Mobutu to seek approval before showing up.
"I imagine that he will not arrive incognito. I assume that we would be informed," the spokesman said.

Mobutu has spent long periods in recent months at his palatial mansion in the smart French Riviera resort of Roquebrune Cap Martin, near Nice. He has been recuperating from prostate cancer surgery and obtaining medical treatment at a hospital in nearby Monaco.
France has maintained close political and economic ties with Zaire as with its numerous other former colonies in Africa.
The setback in Zaire prompted Lionel Jospin, leader of France's opposition Socialists, to level campaign charges that Paris's Africa policies had failed.
